newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA SAYS NO DIPLOMATIC TIES PLANNED FOR IRAQ.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA SAYS NO DIPLOMATIC TIES PLANNED FOR IRAQ.

text.p: South Africa denied on Tuesday that President Nelson Mandela's government was contemplating diplomatic ties with Iraq.

The foreign ministry said no inferences should be drawn from a South African fact-finding mission to the Gulf state this week, despite reports that the trip was a prelude to ending President Saddam Hussein's diplomatic isolation.
"The reports are unfortunate because the aim was not to establish diplomatic relations," a ministry official told Reuters.

"But the fact is that with the expanding nature of our relations around the world we are increasingly called on to take stances on countries such as Iraq...We wanted to apprise ourselves of the situation on the ground," the official said.
An Iraqi opposition group, critical of the South African visit, this week sent Mandela a letter appealing to him not to grant diplomatic status to Baghdad.

The Iraqi National Congress, based in London, urged Mandela to use his "special voice in international affairs" to speak out against the alleged human rights abuses in Iraq, and to help end Saddam's "reign of terror".

South Africa's foreign ministry said its two-man delegation travelled to Iraq as part of a wider Middle East tour (including Jordan, Kuwait, Tel Aviv) and had advised various Gulf countries of the visit to Baghdad in advance.
In Iraq they met government officials as well as non- governmental organisations and foreign diplomats resident in Baghdad, the ministry said.
The delegation also visited South Africa's newly-established representative office in the West Bank town of Ramallah.
